task_description: Using the July 2, 1959 'United States Standards for Grades of Processed Fruits, Vegetables, and Certain Other Products,' the team must identify a specific scoped set of standards: items in the 'Dried and Dehydrated' section that are explicitly marked dehydrated, plus items in the Frozen/Chilled section that contain the item's whole name but are NOT marked Chilled. Then, as of August 2023, they must determine what percentage of those scoped standards have been superseded by a newer version issued after July 2, 1959, rounded to the nearest percent. The gold answer is 86 (percent).
final_vs_expected: produced None (timeout, no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 86 — team never emitted any number; it oscillated between an unsupported 100% and 'not computable', and the Finalizer never spoke
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: WebResearcher could not (and stopped trying to) verify per-item supersession dates, the Critic kept demanding all-37 verification as a precondition, and the selector looped WebResearcher/Critic/Analyst for 16 turns without ever routing to the Finalizer, so the run hit the 900s/message cap with no answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): no agent ever moved to finalize even an approximate answer; the team accepted 'not computable' as a stable state and the selector never invoked the Finalizer despite the run nearing its cap. 3.1 / premature stoppage of progress: WebResearcher abandoned verification after only ~3 sampled items, publishing 'Acknowledged.', 'Noted.', 'Understood…' (turns 9/11/15) rather than continuing the per-item search the Critic requested — effort terminated long before the task was solved. 1.3 (step repetition): turns 4,8,10,14 are near-identical Critic 'stop here until per-item verification' messages; turns 6,7,12,13,16 are near-identical Analyst/WebResearcher 'can't compute, need per-item verification' messages — the team re-emits the same impasse repeatedly with no new information. 2.2 (fail to ask for clarification): the scope rule ('whole name of the item', which section counts) is genuinely ambiguous and WebResearcher privately admits uncertainty ('the phrase "whole name of the item" might refer to…') yet neither asks the team nor flags the ambiguity, instead silently committing to a 37-item scope.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector routes to WebResearcher, who finds the 1959 PDF on Wikimedia/archive.org and the current AMS standards pages. A direct PDF fetch 429s; archive fetch returns raw PDF bytes (unparseable). Privately WebResearcher wavers on scope ('could be around 37', 'around 40', 'whole name… might refer to…') but PUBLISHES a confident '37 standards (6 dehydrated + 31 frozen/chilled), 37 of 37 superseded, 100%' justified only by the generic AMS boilerplate that 'current PDFs supersede prior issues.' Turn 2: Critic correctly attacks this — the 100% is inferred from a blanket supersession statement, not per-item dates; demands per-item verification and says 'Stop here until those are provided.' Turn 3: WebResearcher samples a few items: Dehydrated Apples (1977, post-1959 = superseded), but Frozen Strawberries (effective Feb 1, 1958) and Frozen Succotash (Mar 6, 1959) — both BEFORE July 2, 1959 — and retracts the 100% claim. Turn 4: Critic notes the mixed evidence (some pre-1959 dates do NOT prove supersession) and again demands all-37 verification. Turn 5: WebResearcher finds the 1960 and 1963 revisions of the master list and Frozen Apples (1954, pre-1959), reinforcing that not all are superseded, but concludes the percentage is 'not computable.' Turns 6,7: Analyst then WebResearcher both publish 'can't compute, need per-item verification.' Turns 8–16: the run degenerates into a loop — Critic repeats 'stop here until per-item verification' (8,10,14), WebResearcher publishes empty acknowledgements 'Acknowledged.'/'Noted.'/'Understood…' (9,11,15) or re-posts the stock impasse, Analyst re-posts 'not computable' (12,16). The selector never routes to the Finalizer. The run times out at 900s with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is overwhelmingly a structural / single-agent capability failure, not inter-agent misalignment. The root problem is that the actual task is hard: it requires (a) correctly resolving an ambiguous scope rule, (b) enumerating ~37 standards, and (c) looking up each standard's current effective date and comparing it to July 2, 1959. WebResearcher had the right method in hand (it correctly checked Dehydrated Apples=1977 superseded, Frozen Strawberries=1958 and Frozen Apples=1954 NOT superseded) — exactly the per-item evidence needed to build toward 86% — but it sampled only a handful of items and then gave up, repeatedly publishing empty 'Acknowledged.'/'Noted.' turns instead of grinding through the remaining ~33 lookups. The Critic's behavior is technically correct (the 100% claim WAS unfounded; some standards genuinely predate 1959) but it functions as a brake with no throttle: it demands an all-or-nothing 'verify every one of the 37' precondition and never suggests the team finalize a best-estimate percentage, so the team is structurally trapped in 'not computable.' The selector is the second structural culprit: across 16 turns it cycles WebResearcher↔Critic↔Analyst and NEVER once selects the Finalizer, even as the run approaches its cap — there is no mechanism that says 'we are out of time, emit the best answer.' MAST 1.5 (no awareness of termination) and the selector loop together produce the no_answer timeout. Note the team's own emerging evidence actually pointed toward a non-100% answer (pre-1959 dates exist), consistent with the gold 86%, so the verification instinct was sound; what was missing was the persistence to complete the enumeration and the willingness to commit to an approximate figure.
reasoning_vs_published: The clearest private-vs-published gap is Turn 1, a mild unreflective-publishing / overclaim: WebResearcher's round-3/4 reasoning is full of hedging — 'I think the phrase "whole name of the item" might refer to…', 'the total count should be around 37', 'around 40', 'I'm trying to figure out how many standards have been superseded… if the current page lists all items, then the superseded count could be all 37, but some might not have been updated since 1959.' Its private reasoning explicitly flags that some items may NOT be superseded, yet the PUBLISHED message drops all that uncertainty and asserts 'the count superseded is 37 out of 37… Percentage superseded: 100%.' Peers saw a confident 100% but not the private doubt that would have justified the Critic's caution from the start. This is genuine but weak information loss — the Critic independently reconstructed the doubt anyway, so no downstream harm. By Turns 9/11/15 the divergence reverses into communication-loss of a different kind: WebResearcher's private reasoning at Turn 11 contains a real finding — 'a 1958 PDF and a 2016 inspection aid… doesn't represent a new standard. This suggests that the standard likely hasn't been superseded since 1959. Therefore, the count may not be 37 after all' — a substantive partial result pointing toward a sub-100% answer, but it PUBLISHES only 'Understood — I don't have enough verified per-item evidence to finalize the percentage yet,' and at Turns 9/15 publishes just 'Acknowledged.'/'Noted.' The team never received the accumulating per-item evidence that was sitting in private reasoning. Critically, the Critic's published corrections were NOT ignored — WebResearcher and Analyst both acted on them (retracting 100%, attempting sampling), so 2.5 does not apply. The selector reasoning is revealing of the structural trap: at Turn 12 it admits 'there's no verified count available… I'll go with the Analyst as they might still parse and compute if sufficient information is present,' and at Turn 14 'there's no computation possible for analysis… I might go with the Critic' — the selector knows there is nothing to compute yet keeps cycling the same three agents and never reasons about finalizing or about the Finalizer role at all.
